result.summary: Adds wallet and RPC support for sending to BIP 352 Silent Payment addresses. It introduces PaymentDestination to represent either a standard destination or a silent payments recipient, selects eligible inputs with accessible private keys to perform ECDH, derives Taproot output scripts dynamically, and persists recipient data in wallet storage so RBF fee bumps can recompute destination outputs. Sending to silent payments addresses is supported via send, sendtoaddress, sendmany, and sendall, while workflows incompatible with private-key derivation or fee bumping (such as PSBTs and external signers) are prevented.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core cannot send funds to silent payment addresses. Unlike regular addresses, silent payment outputs lack a static scriptPubKey and require ECDH derivation against the sender's input private keys, preventing standard coin selection, destination handling, PSBT signing, and transaction fee bumping without specialized wallet mechanics.
evidence: PR description: 'This PR is part of integrating silent payments into Bitcoin Core. It is the second iteration of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28201. Status and tracking for the project is managed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28536'

result.scope_notes: The PR touches sensitive wallet coin selection, signing provider logic, and wallet database schemas, and introduces test framework BIP 352 scanning utilities.
result.changed_since_previous: Refactored CreateRateBumpTransaction to return a util::Expected struct instead of out-parameters, fixed original_change_index fee bumping to reject outputs lacking a destination (such as OP_RETURN), and optimized ConstructTransaction to avoid double-parsing outputs.
result.card: Adds wallet sending and fee-bumping support for BIP 352 Silent Payment addresses across send, sendtoaddress, sendmany, and sendall. Bitcoin Core currently cannot send to silent payment addresses because output scripts must be derived dynamically from input private keys rather than static scriptPubKeys. The change introduces PaymentDestination, adjusts coin selection to ensure secret-derivation-eligible inputs with known keys, persists recipient details to the wallet database to enable RBF output recalculation, and disallows PSBT or external signer workflows. It represents the second iteration of sending support under the silent payments project tracking issue (#28536) and depends on PR 35301.

risk.why: Mistakes in input key tweaking or output script derivation could send funds to unspendable or unrecoverable addresses, resulting in permanent loss of funds.
